output.title: Scope creep is usually a boundary problem
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, scope creep is usually not a motivation problem. It is a workflow boundary problem: the work keeps expanding because nothing says where the task starts, where it stops, and what gets deferred.

The useful decision is not “should I automate everything?” It is: which one recurring task is pulling you away from core work, and does it repeat often enough to describe clearly? Customer questions, invoice data entry, and lead follow-up are good examples. If a task does not have a measurable outcome or a stable enough pattern, automation is probably the wrong move.

If it does repeat, compare three options: keep doing it manually, automate a narrow slice, or hire. That comparison only works when the workflow is bounded. For an owner who has tried ChatGPT but has not wired it into a real process yet, the first step is to name the loop and check whether it can be handled without touching money movement or other high-risk decisions. Human approval stays in place there.

Bareni’s diagnostic starts with that same question: identify the one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and only then define a narrow pilot scope. The hard part is usually admitting the task is vague. That is the point.
